samples.text: The incident was raised as INC0080099 opened at priority P2 against inventory-valuation, shortly after the feed stopped. The first line of enquiry looked upstream for an interruption in the source system, because a stalled overnight run usually means its input never arrived. That line of enquiry was wrong. It closed on a single finding: ERP logs show no interruption during the valuation window. With the source cleared, the team turned to the reference data and found the stale agency code mapping. A manual override let the run continue, and by the end of the day the record showed Asset valuation completed. The override was a stopgap, not a repair, and it is the reason the valuation could finish at all that day. The conclusion for the cluster finance partner is that this is a cost of delivery question, and it should be treated as one. A division that hits its funding target and still misses its surplus by this much is spending more to deliver the same programme than the budget assumed, whether through contractor rates, a change in the mix of work, or costs that fell into the month earlier than planned. A line-by-line view of delivery cost against budget is the first step, showing which items moved and whether the movement is likely to recur. If it is structural, the budget for the rest of the year needs to be rebased. If it is a timing effect, that needs to be stated explicitly, so that the forecast does not carry a correction that will reverse on its own. Either answer is acceptable.
